capabilities.text: Choose a circle, ellipse, parabola or hyperbola
Set the centre (h, k), or the vertex of a parabola
Set a circle's radius
Set an ellipse's or hyperbola's a and b
Set a parabola's focal distance p (vertex to focus)
Open a parabola up, down, left or right
Lay an ellipse's major axis or a hyperbola's transverse axis horizontal or vertical
Type the equation in standard form, such as (x - 2)^2/9 + (y + 1)^2/4 = 1, and have it drawn with its parts
Type the equation in general form, such as 4x^2 + 9y^2 - 16x + 18y - 11 = 0, and have the conic named and drawn
capabilities.note: completing the square is the textbook skill this supports

capabilities.text: Type values as fractions or square roots (a = √5, p = 3/2)
Mark and label the centre
Mark and label the vertices
Mark and label an ellipse's co-vertices
Mark and label the foci
Draw and label a parabola's directrix with its equation
Draw the two directrices of an ellipse or hyperbola
capabilities.note: beyond most US texts; in precalculus books that teach eccentricity

capabilities.text: Draw the major and minor axes (transverse and conjugate for a hyperbola), labelled with their lengths 2a and 2b
Draw a parabola's axis of symmetry with its equation
Draw a hyperbola's asymptotes, labelled with their equations
Draw a hyperbola's central rectangle
Draw the latus rectum, labelled with its length
Show a point P on the curve with its focal radii and their lengths (to both foci, or to the focus and directrix of a parabola)
Write the eccentricity e = c/a
List a, b, c and the relation c^2 = a^2 - b^2 (or a^2 + b^2) beside the figure, worked with the values
Label points with their coordinates or with letters only
Give coordinates exactly (2 + √5, -1) or as rounded decimals
Write the equation on the figure in standard or general form
Load a classic example (orbit, satellite dish, whispering gallery, hyperbola with asymptotes, circle from general form)
capabilities.note: a setup choice that loads the values, as the parity figures' Classic setups

capabilities.text: Set each axis's From, To and Count by
Make the gridlines light, standard, bold or none
Add minor gridlines between the numbered lines
Number the axes, or leave the numbers off
Set the axis labels at the arrow tips (x and y, or typed names)
Write a title
Put a blank line in place of the title for students
Make the labels small, medium or large
Draw it in black and white for photocopying (Print)
A student copy that leaves the parts unlabelled for students to name and find
A student copy that keeps the marked points and leaves the curve off, for students to sketch it
A student copy with a blank line for the equation, to write it from the graph
An answer key line giving the equation, centre, vertices, foci and eccentricity
Drag the centre on the figure to move the conic
